## Verdict

**Kelp** costs least for a team of 12, at **$96 per month**. It has both the lowest per-seat rate ($8) and the only minimum (5 seats) that falls below the team size, so the team pays for exactly the 12 seats it uses. Acme Desk and Fennel HQ both force payment for unused capacity at this headcount.

## Vendors

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $14 | 25 |
| Fennel HQ | $19 | 50 |
| Kelp | $8 | 5 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 12 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Kelp:** minimum 5 < 12, so 12 seats paid. 12 × $8 = **$96 per month**. Effective rate $8.00 per person.
- **Acme Desk:** minimum 25 > 12, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $14 = **$350 per month**. 13 unused seats; effective rate $29.17 per person ($350 ÷ 12).
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 50 > 12, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $19 = **$950 per month**. 38 unused seats; effective rate $79.17 per person ($950 ÷ 12).

Kelp is $254 per month cheaper than Acme Desk and $854 per month cheaper than Fennel HQ — $3,048 and $10,248 respectively over twelve months.

## Risks

Seat minimums, not per-seat rates, drive this result, so the gap is size-sensitive. Acme Desk's $350 is fixed until headcount reaches 25, at which point its effective rate drops to $14 — still above Kelp's $8, so Kelp stays cheaper at any size on this list. Fennel HQ does not reach its list rate until 50 seats and is not price-competitive in this range.

This is a price comparison only. The price list carries no information on features, support tiers, usage limits, or security, so a cheaper seat may buy less product.

All figures assume monthly billing at list price as stated. Annual commitments, negotiated discounts, onboarding fees, and migration costs are not in the source and could change the ranking. Confirm whether minimums bind at signup or only at renewal.
